svg.aria-label: Component diagram of three boundaries. First, the model, Claude in VS Code, whose eleven built-in tools are every one of them struck through as denied: the six file tools Read, Write, Edit, NotebookEdit, Grep and Glob; then the three shells Bash, PowerShell and Monitor, Monitor being a shell because it runs the command it is handed in the same environment Bash does; and last the two output readers BashOutput and TaskOutput, which start nothing and write nothing but hand back the output of work already done, bytes that reached the model without passing the tree boundary, the secret scan or the disclosure screen. Second, the Fettler MCP server, whose boundary comes from .fettler.json and which refuses to write the files that govern it or the model. Third, the filesystem, visible only as the declared trees, with everything else refused as nonexistent.
svg.text: everything the assistant is — and every file that shapes it
one process between the model and the disk
what exists, seen through the declared trees
shares the CLI’s registry — one wiring, one verdict
THE ELEVEN BUILT-INS — DENIED BY permissions.deny
THE ONE ROUTE LEFT — MCP TOOLS
mcp__fettler__* find search read write edit move run …
Use the Fettler tools (mcp__fettler__*) for every
file operation. They are the route, not an option.
There is no working directory: ask roots first.
written only on request: fettle setup --global --deny
REPO LEVEL — the project’s own tree
merged, never clobbered; backup written beside it on first setup
Use the Fettler tools for every file operation.
personal and gitignored — grants made here never appear in a
review, so doctor names its presence (finding 2.13)
fettle serve — the MCP front end
launched by the client, on stdio · learns its trees at launch ·
a changed .fettler.json needs a restart · no shell, anywhere
roots · find · search · read · write · edit · replace
move · copy · delete · new · mkdir · extract · exec
— the one verb a model is never offered: it writes the wiring
run executes declared tasks only, takes no arguments, composes no command
THE BOUNDARY — A PERSON WRITES IT; THE TOOL REFUSES TO
this machine’s own; a name in both files is the overlay’s entirely
the refusals that make it hold
path outside every tree → exit 4 refused
write adds a credential → exit 12 credential
run w/o execute grant → exit 8 refused
outside is refused identically whether or not the file exists,
so a refusal cannot be used to probe the disk — and a model that
could edit its own deny list would have no deny list
can: list read create update rename delete execute
execute reaches the declared tasks and nothing else — never a default,
even in the tree the configuration sits in
a scope replaces what its tree grants; the most specific scope decides.
cancelled/ is absent from every find and search, and a direct path is
refused in the same words as a file that was never there
can: list read create update rename delete
the harness’s staging area, declared in the gitignored overlay.
without it, denying the built-in Write closes staging entirely —
doctor names the gap (finding 2.15). no execute: staging, not running
not listable · not readable · not knowable
every path → exit 4, file or no file
the model’s own machine-level configuration lives out here —
reachable by you in an editor, unreachable through the boundary
declares the trees — read once at launch
write the files that govern the model → exit 11
⊘ governed — the tool never writes its own rules
